policies.summary: Pennsylvania has no state siting permit for wind or solar; municipalities (and counties where a municipality has no zoning) regulate them through zoning under the Municipalities Planning Code.
policies.statute_citation: Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, Act of July 31, 1968, P.L. 805, No. 247, §§ 601, 602, 619 (53 P.S. §§ 10601, 10602, 10619)

restrictions.description: Regulatory gap: current zoning ordinance does not address data centers, power generation plants, large-scale/accessory solar, last-mile fulfillment centers, micro-warehouses, or dispensaries, allowing any of them to be built anywhere in the township. Board Chairman Russell Ford emphasized the action was preemptive, not prompted by any pending application. Active as of 2026-09-23, running toward its computed 180-day expiry (~2027-01-09). Adopted via a unanimous June 22, 2026 motion and formalized by resolution at the July 13, 2026 meeting, the moratorium pauses applications for six business types (data centers, power generation plants, large-scale/accessory solar, last-mile fulfillment centers, micro-warehouses, dispensaries) while the township prepares a curative amendment to correct the declared invalidity. No news of an extension, adoption of the amendment, or repeal was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23. Legal basis: Adams Township Board of Supervisors resolution (a follow-up to the June 22, 2026 motion), invoking the municipal curative amendment process under the PA Municipalities Planning Code and declaring the zoning ordinance's exclusion of the six business types 'does not bear a substantial relationship to the public health, safety or morals' of residents, and that a sweeping ban 'cannot pass constitutional muster' and is therefore invalid (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed).

Zoning ordinance lacked provisions for data centers, solar energy, and wind energy. Active as of 2026-07-31; 180-day curative-amendment period from 2026-06-08. No data center application was pending at adoption. Legal basis: Township Council resolution, Municipal Curative Amendment (Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code Section 609.2).

Regulatory gap: the zoning ordinance does not explicitly permit or provide standards for data centers or solar farms ('we don't have the protections in place'); adopted proactively, with no application pending, amid data-center and warehouse-development activity in neighboring Butler and Kline townships. Active as of 2026-09-23. Adopted unanimously on 2026-09-15, covering both data centers and solar farms (plus on-site power generation and accessory uses); the township hired Siana Law as special zoning counsel, with a draft corrective ordinance (addressing noise, buffers, power sources, and community benefits) expected the following month. No application for either use is currently pending. Legal basis: West Mahanoy Township Board of Supervisors resolution invoking the municipal curative amendment process under the PA Municipalities Planning Code, declaring the zoning ordinance invalid as it relates to data centers, solar farms, on-site power generation, and related accessory uses (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed).

projects.description: In 2016, Atlantic Wind submitted a proposal to construct 37 wind turbines in Penn Forest Township on lands owned by the Bethlehem Municipal Authority.

During a series of 21 public hearings between January 2020 and March 2021, residents protested a 75-MW solar energy project proposed by Brookfield Solar I LLC that would span 1,000 acres across 26 different parcels of land in Mount Joy Township.
In November 2023, the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court affirmed the denial of a permit for the Brookview Solar 1 project in Mount Joy Township.
A pumped storage project faced opposition from local groups and environmentalists.
Enel Green Power’s plans to construct a 600-acre solar project in Dover Township encountered local opposition.
In February 2023, the Scranton Zoning Board denied zoning approval to ECA Solar for the construction of a solar farm on West Mountain.
Vesper Energy's Firefly Solar project faced significant local opposition and was ultimately prohibited on agricultural land.
New Leaf Energy’s plans to construct a solar project on 23 acres of land zoned for suburban-residential development in Greenfield Township have encountered local opposition.

In June 2016, the Lehighton Water Authority formally denied Iberdrola Energy’s request to construct three wind turbines on Water Authority property in the area surrounding the Lehighton Borough’s drinking water supply.
In January 2005, Laurel Hill Wind Energy, LLC applied for a special exception to construct a 69-MW wind energy facility on land primarily within the County’s Resource Protection (RP) Zoning district.

In April 2022, the North Annville Township Board of Supervisors denied an application for a conditional use permit for Lebanon Solar I, an 858-acre, 70-MW solar farm proposed by a subsidiary of Enel Green Power.
In September 2024, the Newton Township Supervisors voted to deny a plan by New Leaf Energy, a subsidiary of Borrego Solar Systems, to build around 12,000 solar panels on 24 acres of an old golf club.
In December 2024, the Unity Township Zoning Board voted in a 3-2 decision to deny a special exemption necessary for the 34-acre Ninemile Run Solar project to be constructed.
On July 31, 2024, the Pine Township Zoning Hearing Board rejected an application for a solar project that would have covered 20 acres in the township’s agricultural conservation zone.
In August 2024, Lehman Township’s Zoning Hearing Board voted unanimously to deny a request from Susquehanna Solar to build a 46-acre solar farm in the municipal agricultural district.
On August 21, 2024, the Nanticoke city council unanimously denied an application for a 40-acre solar project that would have been sited near a housing development.

On August 15, 2022, two environmental groups filed an appeal with the Pennsylvania Environmental Hearing Board to challenge Pocono Township’s issuance of a permit to construct an 80-MW solar farm near Swiftwater Creek.
On November 4, 2024, the Palmyra Township Supervisors voted to reject an application by TotalEnergies to construct a 6-MW solar project.
Wilson Solar is seeking to develop an 80-MW solar project on approximately 1,129 acres of land in Erie County.
In 2025, CVE North America proposed the 4.5-MW Derry Township Solar project to be located on approximately 60 acres of privately owned land in a rural neighborhood near New Alexandria.
In 2023, Cornerstone Solar proposed the 200-MW Jefferson Solar project to be located on approximately 730 acres in Jefferson Township.
